title: RADIOISOTOPE THERMOELECTRIC GENERATOR THERMAL MANAGEMENT SYSTEM - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a passive thermal system to regulate the Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator temperature and to provide excess heat to the spacecraft/lander heat management system.Description: For exploration missions, there is a need (In situ resource utilization, deep space missions, long night survival...) to use efficient power generation systems as an alternative to solar panels. Europe is already engaged in developing a Radioisotope Heater Unit (RHU) and the next step is to develop bigger capabilities witha Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (RTG). As RTG is generating significant waste heat, there is an interest to reuse this heatand optimize the thermal control system, hence the whole system. Several thermal management systems with heat recovery are currently under study with the potential capability of receiving waste heat form RHU or RTG. However, interfacing with an RTG and regulatingits temperature is complex and requires a dedicated system for this unit. The goal of the activity is to develop a passive thermal system that regulates the temperature of the RTG and be able to provide excess heat to the spacecraft/lander heat management system viaa dedicated thermal interface. The RTG thermal system requires to operate with less than 5% of the electrical power generated bytheRTG. The heat recovery and the distribution of the RTG thermal energy would increase the overall efficiency of the system by more than 20%. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements consolidation - Technology trade off review - Design and manufacturing of a breadboard demonstrator - Validation testing of the breadboard demonstrator - Way forward for industrializationDeliverables: Breadboard, ReportProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activities in open competition limited to the-non-Large-System Integrators.
